workarounds.symptom: Error trying to open the project in devcontainer in vscode
workarounds.workaround: Fix: Remove devcontainer configuration. Target files: .devcontainer/devcontainer.json, .devcontainer/post-create.sh. This PR and , in a way, by deleting our `.devcontainer` directory. We've only updated these sporadically since they were added, they don't work in their current form, and none of us use them, so I thought it made sense just to remove the files. Codex also came up with a patch to get them working again, though, if we prefer to keep them. (Ref: https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/30910)

workarounds.symptom: Relative imports from a module named `__future__` are treated as future imports
workarounds.workaround: Fix: Treat relative imports from `.__future__` as ordinary imports. Target files: crates/ruff_linter/src/checkers/ast/analyze/statement.rs, crates/ruff_linter/src/checkers/ast/mod.rs, crates/ruff_linter/src/checkers/imports.rs. Treats relative imports from `.__future__` (such as `from .__future__ import x`) as ordinary module imports instead of Python compiler `__future__` statements by checking that `level == 0`. (Ref: https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/30260)

workarounds.symptom: B028 and UP022 fixes break when a keyword argument has a parenthesized value
workarounds.workaround: Fix: Fix fixes that add or remove a keyword argument with a parenthesized value. Target files: crates/ruff_linter/src/fix/edits.rs, crates/ruff_linter/resources/test/fixtures/flake8_bugbear/B028.py, crates/ruff_linter/resources/test/fixtures/pyupgrade/UP022.py. `add_argument` and `remove_argument` used the start of a keyword's parenthesized value as the start of the keyword. That position is after `name=`, so for `category=(DeprecationWarning)` the edit cut the keyword in half. `B028` suggested `category=stacklevel=2, (Deprecatio... (Ref: https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/30189)

workarounds.symptom: `ruff check --verbose` aborts (SIGABRT) when stderr is a pipe that closes early
workarounds.workaround: Fix: Avoid crashing when Ruff logs to a closed stderr pipe. Target files: crates/ruff/src/lib.rs, crates/ruff_linter/src/logging.rs, crates/ruff/tests/cli/lint.rs. When a pipe reader closes stderr, fern tries to report the failed log write to the same pipe and panics. Ruff now ignores stderr write errors when logging, so linting can finish and report diagnostics on stdout. The panic hook also tolerates write failures when reporting a crash. (Ref: https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/30209)

workarounds.symptom: The last version fails to build on FreeBSD
workarounds.workaround: Fix: Fix FreeBSD source builds with libc 0.2.190. Target files: Cargo.lock. Update the locked Mio dependency from 1.0.4 to 1.2.4, which includes the upstream fix for the removed `libc::NOTE_PCTRLMASK` constant. This resolves the compilation failure reported in #30174. (Ref: https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/30176)

workarounds.symptom: Improve D417 missdetection for *args and **kwargs when backslash.
workarounds.workaround: Fix: [`pydocstyle`] Treat backslash-escaped `*args` and `**kwargs` as documented (`D417`). Target files: crates/ruff_linter/src/rules/pydocstyle/mod.rs, crates/ruff_linter/src/rules/pydocstyle/rules/sections.rs, crates/ruff_linter/resources/test/fixtures/pydocstyle/D417.py. Sphinx-style docstrings often escape the stars as `\*args` and `\*\*kwargs`, because a bare `*` starts emphasis in reST. D417 didn't account for that, so it reported those parameters as undocumented even though they were documented. (Ref: https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/29536)

workarounds.symptom: PLE0643 (potential-index-error) counts a starred element of a list or tuple literal as one item
workarounds.workaround: Fix: [`pylint`] Avoid false positive on starred elements (`PLE0643`). Target files: crates/ruff_linter/src/rules/pylint/rules/potential_index_error.rs, crates/ruff_linter/resources/test/fixtures/pylint/potential_index_error.py. `potential-index-error` (`PLE0643`) statically calculates the length of sequence literals (lists and tuples) using the count of AST elements (`elts.len()`). When a sequence contains starred expressions (e.g., `(*a, 9)[2]` or `[*a, *a][2]`), the starred element is counted as a single item, causing `PLE0643`... (Ref: https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/29483)
